trend_source: A US creator's 'Financial Literacy 101' listing where to open a HYSA, Roth IRA, credit cards, ETFs and stocks pulled 373.1k views and 52.8k likes. The format proves people crave a simple starter checklist, but the accounts are American.
title: The Singapore version of Financial Literacy 101 they never taught us
hooks: The viral finance checklist everyone's saving is American, so here's the Singapore version.
Nobody taught us this in school, so let me give you the SG starting line.
Roth IRA and HYSA mean nothing here, so what do we actually use in Singapore?
talking_points: Swap the US HYSA idea for a high yield local savings setup and where to park your emergency fund
Swap the Roth IRA for SRS and topping up CPF for long term, tax advantaged money (check IRAS for current rules)
Instead of naming stocks, talk about starting with broad, low cost diversified funds and regular investing
Point people to official sources for CPF, SRS and tax details before opening anything
cta: Comment START and I'll send you a simple Singapore money checklist to work through this week.
why_it_works: It rides a proven checklist format while honestly fixing the fact that the original accounts don't exist here, which is exactly what confused SG viewers need.
how_to_film: Talk to camera holding up fingers as you count off each swap. Open with the 'it's American' line immediately. Keep it fast, one point per breath, on screen text mirroring each swap.
author: @josefromzero

trend_source: A US creator citing a study that 48% of paychecks are spent within 48 hours got 210.2k views and 33.5k likes. The panic about living paycheck to paycheck clearly resonates, though the study is American.
title: If your salary disappears 48 hours after payday, do this
hooks: If your pay is gone two days after payday, you don't have a money problem, you have a system problem.
Half of some people's salary vanishes within 48 hours, and I get why.
Payday feels great for two days, then what?
talking_points: Automate a transfer out on payday before you can touch it, so saving isn't a willpower fight
Separate needs, wants and future you into different accounts
Build a starter emergency buffer before anything fancy
Only invest what's left after the buffer, so a bad month doesn't force you to sell
cta: Comment PAYDAY and I'll walk you through a simple pay yourself first setup.
why_it_works: The paycheck-to-paycheck feeling is universal and the numbers proved it stops the scroll, and the fix is genuinely useful rather than fear-mongering.
how_to_film: Start with the hook deadpan to camera. Use a simple three account visual or on screen text. Keep tone empathetic, not preachy.
author: @kellykakers

trend_source: A US creator explained personal finance using Calico Critters toys and three 25 year old besties with different debt and habits, hitting 38.4k views and 9.9k likes with 790 shares. The relatable 'same income, different outcomes' story is what carries it.
title: Three friends, same income, wildly different futures
hooks: Three friends earn the exact same salary and end up in totally different places, here's why.
Same paycheck, opposite outcomes, and it comes down to a few habits.
A pay rise won't save you if your lifestyle rises faster.
talking_points: Friend A keeps her lifestyle steady and invests the extra income
Friend B upgrades everything the moment income rises, so nothing is left to grow
The real difference isn't income, it's the gap between what you earn and what you spend
Direct that gap into consistent long term investing rather than lifestyle upgrades
cta: Which friend are you right now? Tell me in the comments.
why_it_works: The three-friends story is a proven, shareable device and honestly illustrates lifestyle inflation without shaming anyone.
how_to_film: Use three labelled cups, sticky notes or props for the three friends. Open with the hook then physically move 'money' between them. Fast, playful pacing.
author: @keeliecreative

trend_source: A US creator's story on why 95% of rich families lose it all by the third generation, using systems over money, hit 70.2k views with 696 shares. The 'grandfather builds, son spends, grandson begs' line drives the reach.
title: Why most family wealth vanishes by the third generation
hooks: The grandfather builds it, the son spends it, the grandson begs, and it's more common than you think.
Most family fortunes don't survive to the grandkids, and money isn't the reason.
Handing your kids money without teaching them is like handing car keys to someone who can't ride a bike.
talking_points: Wealthy families pass down systems and habits, not just cash
Teach kids to manage small amounts well before they inherit anything big
Structure protection so a death or illness doesn't force the family to sell assets
A proper plan, will and adequate coverage keeps the next generation from starting at zero
cta: Book a quick call if you want to build a plan your family can actually carry forward.
why_it_works: The generational wealth story is aspirational and shareable, and it honestly opens a conversation about estate planning and protection without hype.
how_to_film: Tell it as a story to camera, calm and slow. Open with the 'grandfather builds' line. Let each beat land with a pause.
author: @wealth_xplained

Everyone wants the outcome, nobody talks about the price of entry.
You want peace? Then let's talk about clearing your debt first.
talking_points: Want growth: you need to invest consistently, not perfectly
Want peace: clear high interest debt before chasing returns

Match each goal to one concrete action you can take this month

author: @justtonch

trend_source: A US creator's 'finance for the girls' clip on opening Roth IRAs and IRAs got 29.2k views and 4k likes. It shows demand for beginner retirement account guidance, but the accounts are American.

Inside these, you still need to invest, not just leave cash sitting
Start small and automate so it becomes a habit, not a chore

trend_source: A UK creator's four financial milestones for your 20s hit 46.2k views and 3.7k likes. The milestone checklist works, though the ISA and UK figures need localising.
title: Financial milestones to hit in your 20s, Singapore edition
hooks: Four money milestones for your 20s, adapted for Singapore.
By the end of your 20s I'd want you to have hit these four things.
A stocks and shares ISA doesn't exist here, so here's our version.
talking_points: Build an emergency fund of around 3 to 6 months of expenses depending on your dependents
Clear high interest consumer debt like credit cards and buy now pay later
Start investing regularly through a local brokerage or regular investment plan instead of an ISA
Get basic insurance in place early while it's cheaper, so one setback doesn't wipe your progress
cta: Save this and check off how many you've already hit.
why_it_works: The milestone list is a proven save-worthy format and honestly adapts foreign accounts to Singapore realities.
how_to_film: Count on fingers, one milestone per beat, on screen numbered text. Open with the 'four milestones' hook. Confident, upbeat pace.
author: @miarosemcgrath

Growing up around good money habits is a head start most of us didn't get.
Your mindset about money matters as much as how much you make.
talking_points: When your pay rises, keep spending steady and invest the difference
Price purchases in hours of your life, not just dollars
Saving in a plain account isn't the same as investing for growth
These habits compound far more than one lucky windfall

They invested consistently instead of letting cash sit idle

trend_source: US creator Humphrey Talks' 'controversial take: pay off the 3% mortgage early' hit 129.4k views, 2x his usual, with 106 comments. The debate between math and peace of mind is what drives engagement.
title: Paying off a cheap home loan early: dumb or smart?
hooks: Everyone says never pay off a cheap home loan early. I think it's more nuanced.
The spreadsheet says keep the loan. Peace of mind says otherwise.
You can be great at math and still choose to sleep better at night.
talking_points: Mathematically, staying invested often wins over a long horizon
But you don't get a redo on your bad years if a layoff hits
Clearing the loan removes a fixed obligation entirely, not just lowers it
The right answer depends on your job stability, dependents and how you sleep
